pull.title: fuzz: torcontrol: drive the control connection over a mocked socket
pull.body:
The `torcontrol` fuzz target hands made-up replies straight to the `TorController` callbacks, and caps reply lines at 16 characters. As a result, most success paths can't be reached, and the code that parses the control port (`ProcessBuffer()`, `ReceiveAndProcess()`) never runs.

This rewrites the target around a fake Tor on the other end of a real `TorControlConnection`, connected through `DynSock`. Replies go over the wire. The fake Tor answers each command the controller sends with a reply of the matching shape, so inputs can complete the whole handshake: PROTOCOLINFO, authentication (including SAFECOOKIE), GETINFO and ADD_ONION. The harness also checks that reply data never splits a command or injects a new one.

The first commit fixes `DynSock::Wait()`, which deleted its own socket. The bug has been there since #30205; this target is the first caller.

### Testing

Line coverage of `src/torcontrol.cpp` goes from 52% on master to 81% after a 10-minute local run. The master number is from the qa-assets corpus. Most of what remains is the controller thread itself, which the harness replaces, and socket errors that `DynSock` can't produce.

The input format changes, so the corpus in qa-assets needs a refresh.

test: fix DynSock::Wait deleting its own socket

Wait() wrapped `this` in an owning shared_ptr to call WaitMany(), so the
socket was deleted once that temporary went out of scope.

Random replies almost never got past PROTOCOLINFO. Answer the oldest
unanswered command with a reply of the matching shape, including the
SAFECOOKIE server hash, so inputs can walk the whole handshake. Also
assert that reply data never splits or injects a command.
